ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must be conducted against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs' sanctions list. Additionally, all beneficial owners, directors, and senior officers must be screened for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) as defined by FATF Recommendation 12, including domestic and foreign PEPs, their family members, and close associates. The screening must be performed at onboarding, on a continuous basis (at least quarterly), and upon any change in ownership or control. Results must be documented and retained for at least five years. Any positive hit triggers enhanced due diligence, and if sanctions are confirmed, immediate reporting to KoFIU and the Financial Services Commission is required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office (Internet Registry Office - iro.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Korean (Hangul). English names may be used as a secondary name but must be transliterated into Hangul. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) a distinctive element, (2) a description of the business purpose, (3) the corporate form (e.g., 주식회사), and (4) optional additional words.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Registry Office within 14 days of rejection. The appeal must include a written explanation of why the name is not confusingly similar, along with any supporting evidence such as trademark registrations or prior use. The Registry Office must respond within 30 days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Administrative Court within 90 days of the denial.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an equity crowdfunding portal, a virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible. The Financial Services Commission requires a physical office in Korea with dedicated staff and compliance infrastructure. The office must be accessible for regulatory inspections and must have a registered address for service of legal process.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High risk. The Financial Services Commission and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit conduct regular and unannounced on-site inspections. The registry may also conduct physical inspections to verify the existence of the office. The inspection checklist includes: presence of employees, physical signage, office equipment, and compliance records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Korean Commercial Act (Act No. 10366, as amended), particularly Articles 289, 291, 292, 295, 317 and 320 governing the formation, notarization of Articles, payment for shares, and incorporation registration of a Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation); Korean Notary Public Act; Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act (FSCMA, Act No. 16847, as amended), particularly Articles 335-3 through 335-14 governing registration as a small investment brokerage business and the operation of an online equity crowdfunding portal; Enforcement Decree of the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act; Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Korean AML Act); Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Court Registration Office of the competent District Court under the Court Administration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea; online submission through IROS (Internet Registration System) or physical filing at the registry with territorial jurisdiction over the registered head office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation (Corporate Registration Application) accompanied by notarized Articles of Incorporation, capital subscription payment certificate, consents of directors and auditor, corporate seal imprint certificate, and related prescribed court forms.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-in capital is required for a Chusik Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act. The incorporators may fix any capital amount in the Articles, but full payment must be made into a blocked capital subscription account at a Korean bank before the registration application is filed. The blocked capital subscription account is released after the court completes the incorporation registration. For the regulated equity crowdfunding business, the company must separately satisfy the paid-in capital threshold prescribed by the FSCMA Enforcement Decree for a small investment brokerage business (currently applied by the FSC/FSS in the relevant capital schedule, with a common floor of KRW 500 million for a dedicated small investment broker, or a higher amount if the portal seeks broader financial investment authorization), and must at all times maintain investor funds in a separate domestic bank escrow account. Client monies received through the crowdfunding portal must not be commingled with corporate operating funds and must be released only upon lawful settlement or withdrawal in accordance with FSCMA rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [KOREAN BUSINESS NAME] (the

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: HomeTax at www.hometax.go.kr for VAT and corporate tax registration; Korea Customs Service operates UNI-PASS at www.unipass.customs.go.kr for export clearance and zero-rating evidence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident entity obtains its Korean Tax ID (Business Registration Number) by filing the statutory Application for Business Registration with the district tax office that has jurisdiction over the Korean business location, or, in the case of a foreign electronic-service supplier without a Korean establishment, by completing Overseas Electronic Service Supplier (OESS) VAT registration on HomeTax. The filing must be accompanied by the certified and apostilled constitutional documents of the foreign entity, a board resolution or power of attorney naming a Korean tax representative, the Financial Services Commission license or authorization for the equity crowdfunding portal, and evidence of the designated Korean business place. For a non-resident that only has Korean-source withholding obligations and no registration duty, NTS will assign a non-resident taxpayer identification number through the International Tax Division; however, a licensed Chusik Hoesa operating a crowdfunding portal is necessarily a domestic VAT corporation and must obtain the BRN before commencing services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Korean tax system does not provide any check-the-box or elective transparent classification. A Chusik Hoesa is always a taxable domestic corporation; hybrid mismatch rules are mandatory and non-elective. The only possible elections are ordinary fiscal-year or consolidated return elections, not entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic Korean businesses have no monetary VAT registration threshold and must register from the commencement of business. Foreign non-resident electronic service suppliers are statutorily required to register for VAT when their annual taxable electronic-service sales to Korean customers exceed KRW 100,000,000. A small-business simplified VAT taxpayer regime applies domestically to entities with annual taxable turnover below KRW 80,000,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices must be issued through the NTS electronic tax invoice (e-tax invoice) system, either directly on HomeTax or via NTS-certified ERP or accounting software connected by API or web service. The electronic invoice must be transmitted to the NTS by the invoice issuance date, and the NTS database assigns a digital tax invoice number and status that serves as an anti-fraud validation stamp. For export transactions, the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS declaration must be cleared before goods depart Korean territory, and the export clearance number must be linked to the VAT zero-rated tax invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The 0% VAT rate applies to goods physically exported from Korea under a customs export declaration and to services supplied for use or benefit wholly outside Korea, including qualifying offshore digital services that are not consumed by a person in Korea. The taxpayer must prove the exported subject matter crossed Korean customs, the counterparty is a non-resident user or buyer, and the consideration is received in foreign exchange. For equity crowdfunding portal services, the fees earned as intermediary compensation may qualify as zero-rated offshore services only where the issuer or investor is non-resident and the service is actually performed for benefit outside Korea; purely Korean-facing crowdfunding services are taxable at standard rate or VAT-exempt financial service, not zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) via UNI-PASS with export declaration number
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from Korea
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by a Korean foreign-exchange bank or other foreign-exchange transaction evidence
Foreign-exchange repatriation confirmation or proof of external currency deposit account when export proceeds are retained abroad under permitted FTA transactions
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: On audit, NTS and Korea Customs Service cross-match the export declaration, electronic tax invoice, bill of lading, and foreign-exchange remittance records. If zero-rating is not sustained, NTS reassesses 10% VAT, applies statutory additional penalties under the Value-Added Tax Act (generally 40% of the under-reported standard tax amount, plus fixed penalties for false electronic invoices), and imposes interest for uncollected tax. Fraudulent zero-rating claims are referred to prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, carrying imprisonment up to three years or a fine up to KRW 30 million, or up to five years and KRW 50 million for habitual or gross evasion, with retrospective clawback of refunded VAT and recovery of all penalties from the portal operator or its representative.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Korea Customs Service as supervisory and border controls participants under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a highly liberalized yet fully declaratory and surveillance-intensive foreign exchange regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree. The Korean won is generally convertible for residents and non-residents on current account items including trade settlement, service remuneration, dividends, royalties, and ordinary transfers. Capital account transactions, including direct equity investment, cross-border loans, acquisition of securities, and foreign currency deposit conversions, are not prohibited but are subject to mandatory reporting via the Foreign Exchange Information System (FIX) or through a designated foreign exchange bank, with post-reporting accepted only where the statute permits. Non-resident shareholders of a Chusik Hoesa may repatriate dividends after corporate resolution, withholding tax settlement, and submission of audited financial statements, without a separate conversion license for profit remittance if the underlying investment was lawfully reported. However, the BOK and MOEF retain emergency powers to restrict convertibility, impose maximum maturities, require prior approval, or mandate surrender during financial market crisis. In practice, all inward and outward FX flows must be substantiated by invoices, contracts, customs declarations, tax filings, and bank forms, because the banking system automatically transmits every FX transaction to the authorities. This means the rate and time of KRW conversion are freely negotiated with the bank, but the underlying economic reality must be completely documented. Retention of export proceeds in foreign currency is allowed, yet all proceeds must enter through a licensed bank account and be traceable to the relevant export declaration, making a fully documentable treasury trail the central risk management requirement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be received into a domestic foreign exchange bank account within the contractually agreed payment term and, in any case, no later than 180 days from the date of export declaration unless the designated bank grants an extended settlement period due to justifiable commercial reasons. There is no general mandatory conversion ratio; exporters may retain 100% of qualified export proceeds in foreign currency accounts. When conversion to KRW is chosen, the bank executes the transaction at the published market rate and records the settlement in the Foreign Exchange Information Network. Failure to repatriate export proceeds by the deadline without an approved extension triggers the MOEF's non-performance review and may result in administrative penalties or revocation of the exporter's designation as a foreign exchange bank counterparty.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Very low. Offshore digital EMI providers, including clearly regulated foreign payment institutions such as Wise, Revolut, and Airwallex, are not licensed to operate as banks or foreign exchange service providers in South Korea under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act. They cannot file mandatory reports to the Foreign Exchange Information System, cannot lawfully hold domestic escrow balances for a regulated equity crowdfunding portal, and would not qualify as a designated foreign exchange bank. Using a non-licensed EMI for capital collection or investor disbursement would practically constitute unlicensed cross-border payment activity and expose the Chusik Hoesa to regulatory suspension. The only viable architecture is a traditional commercial banking relationship with a Korean licensed foreign exchange bank, supplemented by a domestic licensed escrow arrangement for investor funds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a regulated online investment-linked financial business, at least one departing statutory director of the Chusik Hoesa must appear physically in-branch for a face-to-face KYC interview with the bank's compliance officer and the designated relationship manager. Remote consular notarization and apostilled legalisation of board resolutions may be used to authorize a local non-director signatory, but the first director identity verification cannot be completed remotely in the post-regulatory modernization environment. Video-linked interviews may supplement the meeting but can never replace the physical appearance required by Korean anti-money laundering practice for high-risk special-license entities. The bank will review the nominated signatory's identity in real time, verify the corporation's registered seal, and retain a branch visit record as part of the account opening files.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity created by a multi-layer cross-border shareholding chain above the Chusik Hoesa and possible nominee shareholder arrangements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A notarized and apostilled chain-of-ownership certification comprising: the corporate certificate of incorporation and register of directors for every entity in the ownership chain, extracts from the Korean registry and foreign registries dated within the last three months, personal identification document for each ultimate natural-person beneficial owner, sworn source-of-funds declarations supporting the original equity injection, tax residency certificates or CRS returns of the ultimate owners, and a fully annotated group structure chart traced down to the natural person level.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High risk of commingling investor escrow funds with operational treasury because the company is an equity crowdfunding portal that legally handles investor money.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A fully executed escrow agreement with a licensed domestic financial institution proving segregation of investor funds; an independent auditor's confirmation letter detailing daily reconciliation and non-commingling protocols; the portal's written AML/CFT and transaction monitoring procedures; predefined sweep instructions for investor proceeds; and monthly reconciliation statements signed by both the portal and the escrow bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large numbers of small-value inbound investor remittances creating an apparent smurfing or layered payment pattern through multiple digital channels.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: An investor-level KYC/CDD ledger containing national ID or recognized bank-verified identification for each investor, evidence that every payment originated from a matching real-name financial account, batch transaction monitoring reports showing anti-smurfing alerts and their disposition, the licensed portal's investment limit reports, and a complete fund-flow mapping from investor deposit through escrow to final equity issuance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse media exposure because the portal facilitates startup funding for digital content and could funnel proceeds from high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A professional enhanced due diligence report from a licensed third-party screening vendor, negative news and open-source intelligence search evidence, KOFI UN sanctions list and PEP screening results for all directors and material shareholders, an IP licensing and royalty routing explanation, customer geographic segmentation, and written remedial procedures for any red-flag jurisdictions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injection follows the Foreign Investment Promotion Act reporting route. The non-resident shareholder submits the prescribed foreign investment report with the chosen designated bank and obtains an investment registration certificate. The actual remittance then flows via SWIFT MT103 to the Chusik Hoesa's own capital escrow account at the Korean bank using the purpose category for direct equity participation in a domestic company. The bank confirms receipt and issues a certificate of capital verification upon matching the remitter name, account, and investment report number. For a crowdfunding portal, any inbound funds intended as operating capital must be separated from investor subscription funds; therefore a distinct capital escrow account is mandatory. The bank will apply the normal surrender or conversion rules if the inflow is denominated in foreign currency, and will require the remitter to identify the source account and the investment vehicle.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for platform operations, dividend payments, technology royalties, and startup funding flows must clear through Korean licensed foreign exchange banks. SWIFT MT103 is the standard rail for direct low to mid-value vendor and shareholder payments; documentary collections such as DP or DA are used where clean payment is not yet due; commercial letters of credit issued as MT700 or MT707 are recommended for larger import-linked trade settlements. Each cross-border disbursement requires a purpose code, supporting invoice or contract, evidence of underlying economic substance, and customs documents where goods are involved. Domestic KRW payables should settle through the Korean FPS or bank transfer network, while KRW/foreign currency liquidity clearing between domestic and offshore parties is ultimately settled in KRW through the BOK Wire+ system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts with a licensed Korean bank up to 12 months tenor, permitted only against real underlying trade receivables, dividend receipts, or investment capital flows
Cross-currency swaps to monetize or hedge long-term non-KRW debt and equity-related forex exposure
FX collar and participating forward structures used for hedging the portal's USD/KRW operational and development expenses

Onshore deliverable options and FX swaps within the real-demand rule, while non-deliverable forwards remain restricted for domestic corporate use and are not generally accessible to a non-financial crowdfunding portal

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regular General Meeting of Shareholders for adoption of annual financial statements and appointment/ratification of directors and statutory auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records office; minutes are retained at the registered office and are not routinely filed with a regulator unless a special resolution requires commercial registration amendment; shareholders may inspect under the Korean Commercial Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of each fiscal year; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, no later than 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be subject to an administrative fine under the Korean Commercial Act of up to KRW 20,000,000 (approx USD 15,000) for unjustified failure to convene the meeting; a court may order convening on shareholder application; continued non-compliance can support corporate dissolution proceedings; no administrative strike-off exists in the Korean corporate registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit report and audited financial statements filed with the Financial Services Commission via the Financial Supervisory Service electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) / Financial Supervisory Service (FSS), DART e-filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed before the annual general meeting; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, the audited report is due within the statutory external-audit filing window under the External Audit Act, generally not later than six weeks after receipt of the audit report and in no event later than the statutory AGM deadline; listed issuers file an audited annual business report within 90 days after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: FSC may impose administrative fines up to KRW 30,000,000 for late or omitted filing; wilful false audit disclosure carries criminal penalties up to three years imprisonment or KRW 30,000,000; for an FSC-licensed equity crowdfunding portal, unresolved non-compliance may trigger license suspension and ultimately license revocation, which function as the administrative forfeiture equivalent; no Companies Registry strike-off applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporation tax return and local income tax surcharge return, including tax-basis financial statements and shareholder/paid-in-capital schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) for corporation tax; local government tax authority for the local income tax surcharge
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, by 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers statutory penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes, generally 20% of the unpaid tax for late filing, 10% for simple under-reporting and 40% for intentional concealment; unpaid tax accrues delinquency interest at the statutory daily rate; NTS may seize bank accounts and assets, suspend the business registration, and after prolonged unresolved delinquency seek court-ordered dissolution; there is no automatic corporate-register strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual business report and financial condition report of the equity crowdfunding portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) via the Financial Supervisory Service e-reporting system; submission may be coordinated with Korea Securities Depository for crowdfunding settlement records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of each business year; by 31 March for a 31 December fiscal year-end; quarterly report filings, if required by FSC crowdfunding regulations, are due within 45 days after the end of each quarter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: FSC may impose administrative fines up to KRW 100,000,000 for false or late filing; the FSC may suspend the crowdfunding license, impose a corrective order, or revoke the license if the breach is not cured within the prescribed cure period; criminal penalties apply for wilful misstatement; license revocation is the operative administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AML compliance report, customer due diligence refresh, and beneficial ownership attestation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) under the Financial Transactions Reports Act; also supervised by the Financial Supervisory Service for AML internal controls
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within three months after fiscal year-end (by 31 March for calendar-year entities); a 30-day supplementary reporting window applies after any material change in beneficial ownership, shareholding transfer, or control event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to KRW 30,000,000 per violation under AML/customer-due-diligence rules; continued deficiencies can lead to business suspension or license revocation of the crowdfunding portal; wilful evasion of reporting obligations may lead to criminal prosecution; no corporate-register strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial registration amendments and foreign investment change reports (when share transfers affect registered capital, control, or non-resident ownership)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipal Commercial Registration Court / Registry Office; for foreign investment matters, the reporting venue is the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) One-Stop Support Center or the designated competent authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any transfer, increase, decrease, or control change affecting the registered capital, directors, statutory auditor, or foreign investor status; annual confirmation is not separately filed for a domestic Chusik Hoesa unless a supervisory license condition requires it
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late commercial registration amendment may result in administrative fines up to KRW 5,000,000 and loss of good-faith transfer protection; failure to file a foreign investment change report within 30 days may result in administrative penalties and forfeiture of foreign-investment tax benefits; there is no administrative strike-off by the registry.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent external audit by a certified public accountant under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies is required for any Korean Chusik Hoesa if: (1) total assets equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9.2 million) as at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year; (2) the company is a listed issuer on the Korea Exchange (KOSPI, KOSDAQ or KONEX); (3) the company holds a financial investment business license under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act, including an equity crowdfunding portal, irrespective of asset size; (4) the company is designated by the Financial Services Commission as a public-interest company or as an entity requiring external audit for investor and creditor protection under Article 2 of the External Audit Act and the Enforcement Decree; or (5) the company meets sub-threshold designation criteria in the Enforcement Decree, such as significant outside-shareholder exposure, asset-backed financing arrangements, or a debt-to-equity ratio indicating serious financial risk, and the FSC orders an audit. The auditor must be registered with the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants and independent of the company and its controlling shareholders.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS), which are in substance identical to IFRS, apply to listed companies and financial investment business entities, including an FSC-licensed equity crowdfunding portal; non-public smaller Chusik Hoesa may apply Korean GAAP (K-GAAP) or the General Purpose Financial Reporting Standards for SMEs issued by the Korean Accounting Standards Board; audited financial statements must be prepared in Korean, reconcile to the statutory tax basis, and include the independent auditor's true-and-fair opinion under the External Audit Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a separate annual UBO registry form for domestic Chusik Hoesa. However, the entity must maintain an up-to-date register of shareholders at its head office, update that register whenever a share transfer or pledge is presented for registration, and include a beneficial ownership refresh in the annual AML/CDD programme of the crowdfunding portal. A material shareholding transfer or control change must be reflected in the register immediately, and where AML-reportable the updated beneficial ownership information must be communicated to the competent financial authority within 30 days. If a non-resident foreign investor is involved, the company or investor must file a foreign investment change report with the designated support centre within 30 days of the transaction. The Korean corporate registry does not require an annual confirmation filing unless the transaction also changes registered capital, directors, statutory auditor, or other register facts.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Statutory Auditor
Register of Pledges / security interests over shares
Minute Book of shareholders' meetings and board of directors' meetings
Register of Charges / mortgages covering secured financing assets, where applicable
General accounting books and tax records required under the Korean Commercial Act

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - 4,000 per annum for standard Korean registered office, company secretarial and mail handling; add USD 12,000 - 35,000 per annum for an FSC-compliant crowdfunding compliance officer, AML service provider and regulatory filing support where license conditions require it.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 25,000 - 60,000 for a full K-IFRS audit of a private Chusik Hoesa above the mandatory audit threshold; USD 50,000 - 120,000 for an FSC-licensed equity crowdfunding portal requiring regulated-entity audit procedures, DART filing coordination and AML/regulatory opinion work.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 21% top marginal rate; progressive schedule is 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million, 19% on taxable income exceeding KRW 200 million up to KRW 20 billion, and 21% on taxable income exceeding KRW 20 billion.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax incentives include tax holidays and 50% corporate tax reductions for foreign-invested enterprises located in Free Economic Zones under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; research and development tax credits up to 20% of qualifying R&D expenses; employment and investment tax credits for start-ups; venture company income reduction under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act; no general patent box regime, but income from developed IP may be reduced through R&D credits and foreign investor incentives.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporation Tax Return for Domestic Corporation filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic portal (hometax.go.kr); the primary return is the annual corporate income tax declaration with supplementary schedules for related-party transactions and withholding remittances.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; interim tax prepayment obligations on the previous fiscal-year profit during the current fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending on December 31, the annual return must be filed and paid by March 31 of the next calendar year; for any other fiscal year-end, within three months after the last day of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification and tax-filing period: corporation name, corporate registration number, head office address, tax year start and end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-controlled Chusik Hoesa, enter the Korean place of effective management and the foreign shareholder tax identification number if registered as a foreign investor; failure to identify foreign controlling shareholders may trigger disclosure penalties under foreign investment and tax law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income statement reconciliation: sales, operating income, non-operating income, and net income before tax as per Korean GAAP or IFRS financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile escrow-related service fees, crowdfunding facilitation commissions, and foreign-source revenue with Korean GAAP; classify revenue from non-resident issuers and investors as domestic-source income if the service is performed or the platform activities operate in Korea.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income adjustments: non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt income, depreciation differences, reserves, and bad-debt adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not deduct deemed contributions or subsidies from foreign parent shareholders unless arm's length; transfer pricing adjustments under Article 4 of the International Tax Coordination Act must be reflected in this reconciliation, otherwise the NTS may upwardly adjust and impose surcharges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base or taxable income calculation and loss carryforward deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the eligible loss carryforward deduction using the statutory limit; a change in 50% or more of shares held by non-resident shareholders may bar loss carryforward under the deemed new-company rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computation by progressive brackets and local income tax surtax at 10% of the national corporate tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify the top marginal rate of 21% and local surtax of 2.1%; no withholding tax offset is available to the Korean entity for dividends paid to foreign shareholders because profit repatriation tax is separate and imposed at shareholder level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, exemption and reduction, and minimum tax: foreign tax credit, research and development credits, employment credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder cannot book the Korean corporation's foreign tax credit personally; credits obtained in Korea reduce corporate tax only, and any intercompany royalties or interest paid abroad must comply with arm's length and have valid withholding tax remitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax remittance schedule for payments to non-residents: dividends, interest, royalties, and service fees paid to foreign shareholders and counterparties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Before declaring overseas dividends or remitting royalties or interest, apply the 22% aggregate statutory withholding rate of 20% national tax plus 2% local surtax unless reduced by a Double Tax Agreement; remit with the National Tax Service within the statutory deadline and file the non-resident tax withholding return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Supplementary schedules and transfer pricing disclosures: disclosure of related-party transactions, local file, master file, and Country-by-Country Report status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mark the extent of foreign related-party transactions and whether filing thresholds are met; cross-border equity crowdfunding transactions between the platform and affiliated special purpose entities require OECD-compliant comparability analysis or local file documentation; omission triggers reportable transaction penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file by the statutory deadline triggers a non-filing surcharge of 20% of unpaid corporate tax; unfaithful or incorrect filing carries a penalty of 10% of underreported tax and 20% of unfaithfully returned tax; daily delinquency surcharges accrue at 0.022% per day after the payment deadline; intentional evasion with false books constitutes criminal tax fraud under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, punishable by imprisonment up to ten years or a fine of one to five times the evaded tax, with NTS blacklisting and public disclosure for habitual evaders.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate statutory dividend withholding tax applicable to non-resident shareholders: 20% national withholding plus 2% local income tax surtax, unless reduced by an applicable Double Tax Agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Korean paying corporation must obtain, before or by the time of payment, a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign shareholder's competent tax authority; the shareholder must submit the Korea-specific withholding tax treaty relief application through HomeTax, including a beneficial ownership declaration certifying that the recipient is not a nominee or conduit and that any Limitation on Benefits clause is satisfied; the paying corporation may apply the reduced treaty rate at source only after the treaty relief application is accepted, otherwise the NTS will collect the full statutory withholding and assess delinquency surcharges; relief may be denied where the foreign shareholder lacks substance, the certificate is not in the recipient's name, or the shareholding structure is considered treaty shopping.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rates on cross-border interest and royalties are also 22% aggregate, composed of 20% national tax plus 2% local income tax surtax; under most Korean Double Tax Agreements, treaty-reduced rates for interest and royalties range from 10% to 15%, but treaty relief still requires a valid Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership proof.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5 billion in annual foreign-related party transactions creates the mandatory Local File and Master File preparation duty; a consolidated multinational group with annual revenue of KRW 1 trillion or more also files a Country-by-Country Report; even below the threshold, the NTS may demand contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation where the Korean entity engages in cross-border transactions with non-resident related parties.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although South Korea does not impose a separate six-box Economic Substance Regulations test, the economic substance doctrine is embedded in treaty abuse rules, transfer pricing analysis and controlled-foreign-company principles; the equity crowdfunding portal, as a regulated financial intermediary, must maintain real decision-making and workforce in Korea, and Core Income-Generating Activities including investor onboarding, issuer due diligence, platform operation, escrow oversight and AML compliance must be performed in Korea; a shell company claiming DTA benefits without such substance will be treated as a conduit and denied treaty protection, and the NTS may re-characterize or disregard intermediary entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean portal books income as non-taxable software royalties to a related foreign company with no employees, fabricates commission expenses for fake crowdfunding leads, omits escrow-based crowdfunding commission income from the taxable base, and files the annual Box 1 through Box 8 return with knowingly false revenue figures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 3(1) of the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, intentional evasion is punishable by imprisonment up to ten years or a fine equal to one to five times the evaded tax; the NTS imposes an unfaithful return surcharge of 20/100 of unreported tax and 10/100 of understated tax under Articles 47-2 and 47-3 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, plus a daily delinquency surcharge of 0.022% from the due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where directors intentionally cause or wilfully connive at the false filing, the corporate veil is pierced under applicable Korean tax and tort principles; directors are jointly and severally liable for the entity's unpaid tax, can have personal bank accounts seized, are subject to a travel ban and NTS blacklisting, and may be sentenced to up to ten years of imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Treaty Abuse and Transfer Pricing Mispricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The foreign ultimate parent is a zero-tax shell with no employees or Core Income-Generating Activities; the Korean Chusik Hoesa claims zero withholding under an improperly applied Double Tax Agreement on dividends and royalties, while its intercompany fees for platform usage are not benchmarked to arm's length, and no Local File or Master File was prepared despite foreign related-party transactions exceeding the KRW 5 billion threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS will deny treaty benefits under the Limitation on Benefits clause of the applicable Double Tax Agreement and adjust taxable income to the arm's length price under Article 4 of the International Tax Coordination Act, imposing an adjustment surcharge of 20% of the corrected tax plus daily delinquency surcharges; failure to prepare and submit transfer pricing documentation attracts additional penalties under Article 11 of the International Tax Coordination Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors as controlling persons are personally liable for the adjusted tax and penalties; the NTS can issue a departure restriction order or travel ban, blacklist the entity and its owners, and a court can pierce the corporate veil to attach the directors' personal assets in Korea; criminal liability under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act may arise if the directors knowingly received distributions from the treaty-abusive structure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Financial Crime and Unauthorized Crowdfunding Solicitation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The portal solicits retail investors in Korea without the required specialized equity crowdfunding license under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act, routes investor funds through ACH escrow accounts without AML surveillance, and fails to file suspicious transaction reports for money laundering through fake equity issuances; the portal functions as an unlicensed securities intermediary.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A violation of the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act online investment-linked financial business registration requirement is punishable by imprisonment of up to five years or a fine of up to KRW 500 million; failure to maintain internal AML controls under the Specific Financial Transaction Information Act attracts administrative fines and criminal imprisonment of up to three years or a fine of up to KRW 30 million; severe cases lead to license revocation and criminal prosecution by the Financial Services Commission.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally face criminal prosecution and imprisonment; courts order forfeiture and recovery of illicit commissions from directors' personal assets; directors are placed on the financial services authority blacklist and receive travel bans preventing departure during criminal investigation; investor restitution claims pierce the corporate veil and hold directors personally liable for losses suffered by retail investors.
